_comment_file: The connection tree, the command palette and the connection editor — everything under apps/desktop/ui/src/features/connections. The editor is the largest surface in the product, and most of its copy is about ONE idea: a value can be set here or inherited from a folder above, and the screen always says which. Keep that vocabulary consistent. 'inherit', 'override' and 'revert' are the three verbs; if your language needs different words for them, pick three and use them everywhere in this file.

punctuation._comment_detail: Separates a statement from the value it is about: 'overrides the value from Datacentre EU-West · 2222'. Also joins the suggested actions on a failure notice. A locale whose readers expect a different glyph may change it; it is punctuation, not copy. The glyph only — the space on either side of it is layout and is added by the code.

tree._comment_: The sidebar. It is 268px wide, so a label that wraps to three lines is a design problem — prefer the shorter phrasing where your language offers one.
tree._comment_label: The accessible name of the tree itself, read out when a screen reader enters the sidebar. Plural: it names the collection, not one connection.
tree.label: कनेक्शन
tree._comment_filterLabel: The accessible name of the same box. Longer than the placeholder on purpose: read aloud with no sidebar around it, 'Filter connections' does not say what is being filtered.
tree._comment_sectionFavourites: A section heading over the connections tagged 'favourite'. The tag itself is user data and is never translated; this heading is.
tree._comment_sectionAll: The heading over the tree proper, below the favourites. 'All' as in 'the whole tree', not 'select all'.
tree.emptyVault: इस वॉल्ट में अभी कोई कनेक्शन नहीं है। शुरू करने के लिए एक बनाएँ।
tree._comment_noMatches: {query} is what the user typed. It is quoted here because it may be a single character, and an unquoted one reads as a typo in the sentence.
tree.noMatches: ट्री में “{query}” से कुछ भी मेल नहीं खाता।
tree._comment_newConnection: A button and a menu item. Imperative in effect: pressing it opens an empty editor. 'New', not 'Add' — nothing is added until Create is pressed.

row._comment_: One row of the tree, at 14px in a narrow column. Every string here also has to survive being read out in sequence, one row after another.
row._comment_expand: Verb, on the chevron of a closed folder. It opens the folder; it does not resize anything.
row._comment_collapse: Verb, on the chevron of an open folder. The opposite of expand.
row._comment_inheritsCount: A badge on a folder: how many fields this folder sets that every entry beneath it takes from it. Very short — it sits in a badge a few characters wide.
row.inheritsHint: इस फ़ोल्डर की वे फ़ील्ड जिन्हें उसके नीचे की हर चीज़ इनहेरिट करती है
row._comment_usedByCount: A badge on a shared credential: how many entries log in with it. Same width constraint as inheritsCount.
row.usedByHint: वे कनेक्शन जो अपना क्रेडेंशियल इसी एंट्री से लेते हैं

menu._comment_: The right-click menu on a row. Each item is a verb the user is about to perform.
menu._comment_connect: Verb: open a session to this connection now.
menu._comment_edit: Verb: open this entry in the editor.
menu._comment_export: Verb, on the menu item that opens the export dialog for this folder or connection — or for the whole vault, when the menu was opened on empty space. The ellipsis marks it as leading to a dialog.
menu._comment_delete: Verb, on the menu item that opens the confirmation. The confirmation has its own button, delete.confirm — the two may need different forms in your language.

delete._comment_: SECURITY-CRITICAL SECTION. Deleting writes the vault at once and nothing can bring the entry back. Do not soften any of it, do not make it more polite, and do not turn a statement of fact into a suggestion.
delete.title: यह एंट्री हटाएँ?
delete._comment_contains: Shown after the entry name when the entry is a folder with things inside it. {count} is everything beneath it, at any depth — not just its immediate children. SECURITY-CRITICAL: the point of the sentence is that the contents go too, which is the part a user does not expect.
delete.contains: {count, plural, one {इसके अंदर # एंट्री है, और वह भी इसके साथ हट जाएगी।} other {इसके अंदर # एंट्रियाँ हैं, और वे भी इसके साथ हट जाएँगी।}}
delete._comment_irreversible: SECURITY-CRITICAL. States two facts: the vault is written immediately, and there is no undo. Both must survive translation. 'in this version' is deliberate — it says the limit is this build, not the design.
delete.irreversible: हटाते ही वॉल्ट तुरंत लिख दिया जाता है। इस संस्करण में इसे पहले जैसा करने का कोई तरीका नहीं है।
delete._comment_confirm: The button that performs the deletion. Imperative. Keep it short and keep it unambiguous — this is the last thing between the user and permanent loss.

move._comment_: Drag-and-drop, and the Ctrl+arrow keyboard equivalent. Everything here is announced to a screen reader through a live region: a sighted user watches the row move, and these sentences are the only thing a blind user gets. Say plainly what happened, in the past tense, and name both ends of the move.
move._comment_inProgressCount: Shown beside the spinner while one reorder is written to the vault, which it does one entry at a time. {done} counts from 0 up to {total}; both are plain counts, not names. Only used when a move takes more than one write — 'inProgress' above covers the single one.
move.inProgressCount: ले जाया जा रहा है… {total} में से {done}
move._comment_undoing: A move is several vault writes. When one of them fails, the ones that already landed are undone one at a time, and this is the status line while that happens. Nothing is being moved anywhere new.
move.undoing: प्रविष्टियाँ वापस रखी जा रही हैं…
move._comment_notUndone: Rare and serious: the move failed, and so did the attempt to undo the part of it that had already been written, so two entries were left in the same position and the tree the user is looking at is not the one in the vault. Keep the second sentence — it is the way out, not reassurance.
move.notUndone: कुछ प्रविष्टियाँ सूची में एक ही जगह साझा कर रही हैं, क्योंकि उन्हें वापस रखना भी विफल रहा। उनमें से किसी एक को दोबारा ले जाने पर क्रम ठीक हो जाता है।
move.failed: एंट्री नहीं ले जाई जा सकी
move._comment_failedAnnounce: The same failure, read out. {reason} is the core's own sentence, already written for a person; it arrives complete and punctuated.
move.failedAnnounce: एंट्री नहीं ले जाई जा सकी। {reason}
move._comment_refuseSelf: Why a drop was refused. Each of these is announced at the moment the drop is released, so it has to make sense with no other context.
move.refuseSelf: कोई एंट्री अपने ही ऊपर नहीं छोड़ी जा सकती।
move.refuseDescendant: फ़ोल्डर को उसी चीज़ के अंदर नहीं ले जाया जा सकता जो उसके अपने अंदर है।
move._comment_refuseNotFolder: Only folders hold other entries. Groups look like folders and do not, which is exactly why this sentence has to be about folders rather than about containers.
move.refuseNotFolder: दूसरी एंट्रियाँ सिर्फ़ फ़ोल्डर ही रख सकता है।
move.refuseGone: वह एंट्री अब ट्री में नहीं है।
move.cancelled: यह मूव रद्द कर दिया गया।
move._comment_movedInto: {name} is the entry that moved and {parent} the folder it went into. Both are user data, in any script, isolated before they arrive.
move.movedInto: “{name}” को “{parent}” के अंदर ले जाया गया।
move._comment_movedToTop: The top level is the root of the tree — no folder above it.
move.movedToTop: “{name}” को सबसे ऊपरी स्तर पर ले जाया गया।
move._comment_movedAbove: {anchor} is the sibling the entry now sits above. 'Above' is a position in the list as it is drawn, not a level of nesting.
move.movedAbove: “{name}” को “{anchor}” के ऊपर ले जाया गया।
move.movedBelow: “{name}” को “{anchor}” के नीचे ले जाया गया।
move._comment_movedOutOf: One level of nesting shallower: the entry left {parent} and is now the parent folder's sibling.
move._comment_atFirst: Nothing moved. Announced when Ctrl+Up is pressed on the first entry of its list — the keyboard equivalent of a refused drop.
move.atFirst: “{name}” अपने स्तर की एंट्रियों में पहले से ही सबसे पहले है।
move.atLast: “{name}” अपने स्तर की एंट्रियों में पहले से ही सबसे आख़िर में है।
move.atTopLevel: “{name}” पहले से ही सबसे ऊपरी स्तर पर है।
move._comment_cannotIndent: Ctrl+Right moves an entry into the folder directly above it. There is no such folder here.
move.cannotIndent: “{name}” के ठीक ऊपर कोई फ़ोल्डर नहीं है जिसके अंदर इसे ले जाया जा सके।
move._comment_movedSeparatorAbove: A separator is the horizontal line a user can draw between two entries to group them. It has no name, so 'the separator' takes the place of the quoted name in these four sentences; {anchor} and {parent} are user data, isolated before they arrive. Everything else in this object applies: past tense, name both ends, say plainly what happened.
move.movedSeparatorAbove: विभाजक को “{anchor}” के ऊपर ले जाया गया।
move.movedSeparatorBelow: विभाजक को “{anchor}” के नीचे ले जाया गया।
move.movedSeparatorInto: विभाजक को “{parent}” के अंदर ले जाया गया।
move.movedSeparatorToTop: विभाजक को सबसे ऊपरी स्तर पर ले जाया गया।

export._comment_: The export dialog: writes the connection tree, or one folder of it, to a file. It says two things before the button because both change whether someone should press it: no password or key is ever in the file, and the file itself is not encrypted.
export._comment_purposeLabel: The first question of the dialog, and the accessible name of the two choices under it: who the exported file is for.
export._comment_purposeRemoterHelp: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Both halves must survive: the passwords ARE in the file, and the file is encrypted with a password the user chooses. 'Only Remoter opens it' is literal — the format is Remoter's own.
export.purposeRemoterHelp: सर्वर पासवर्ड और कीज़ समेत एक .rmtr आर्काइव, आपके चुने हुए पासवर्ड से एन्क्रिप्ट किया हुआ। इसे सिर्फ़ Remoter खोलता है, और सिर्फ़ उसी पासवर्ड से।
export._comment_purposeOtherHelp: SECURITY-CRITICAL. 'No passwords or keys' must be plain and unhedged.
export.purposeOtherHelp: CSV, OpenSSH config या JSON, जिसे दूसरे टूल पढ़ते हैं। कोई पासवर्ड या की नहीं लिखी जाती।

archive._comment_: The export to another Remoter: a .rmtr archive carrying server passwords and keys, encrypted with a password the user sets here.
archive._comment_included: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The heading of a callout: the passwords are in this file. Do not soften it.
archive.included: सर्वर पासवर्ड और कीज़ शामिल हैं।
archive._comment_includedBody: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The consequence of losing the archive password is part of the sentence and must survive translation.
archive.includedBody: ये आर्काइव पासवर्ड से, आपके वॉल्ट जैसे ही एन्क्रिप्शन से एन्क्रिप्ट होती हैं। आर्काइव इम्पोर्ट करने वाले को यह पासवर्ड चाहिए, और अगर यह खो जाए तो फ़ाइल कोई नहीं खोल सकता।
archive._comment_passwordLabel: The password that seals the archive — not the vault's master password and not a server password.
archive.passwordHelp: इसे आर्काइव इम्पोर्ट करने वाले तक फ़ाइल के अलावा किसी और रास्ते से पहुँचाएँ।
archive.passwordMissing: पहले आर्काइव के लिए पासवर्ड चुनें।
archive.mismatch: दोनों पासवर्ड एक जैसे नहीं हैं।
archive.generateFailed: पासफ़्रेज़ नहीं बनाया जा सका। इसके बजाय पासवर्ड लिखें।
archive.ratingFailed: पासवर्ड की मज़बूती नहीं जाँची जा सकी।
archive.tooWeak: सर्वर पासवर्ड रखने वाली फ़ाइल के लिए अनुमान लगाना बहुत आसान।
archive.busy: फ़ाइल एन्क्रिप्ट करके लिखी जा रही है…
archive._comment_doneDetail: {connections} is how many connections are in the archive, {secrets} how many passwords, keys and passphrases, {path} the file (isolated), {size} its size, already formatted.
archive.doneDetail: {path} में {connections, plural, one {# कनेक्शन} other {# कनेक्शन}} और {secrets, plural, one {# पासवर्ड या की} other {# पासवर्ड और कीज़}} लिखी गईं ({size})।
archive._comment_dependenciesTitle: A heading over a list of names: shared credentials and jump hosts from elsewhere in the vault that the exported folder uses, which were put into the archive so it works on its own. {count} is how many.
archive.dependenciesTitle: {count, plural, one {यह भी शामिल है, क्योंकि एक्सपोर्ट इसका इस्तेमाल करता है} other {ये भी शामिल हैं, क्योंकि एक्सपोर्ट इनका इस्तेमाल करता है}}

export.title: कनेक्शन एक्सपोर्ट करें
export._comment_scopeLabel: Which part of the tree to write. The label above a pair of radio buttons.
export._comment_scopeNode: {name} is the folder or connection the dialog was opened on, isolated. 'Everything in it' is what makes the choice different for a folder; for a connection it is harmless.
export._comment_csv: A file format name. Not translated, in any language or script.
export._comment_sshConfig: The name of OpenSSH's client configuration file. 'OpenSSH' is a product name and 'config' is how its users say it; neither is translated.
export._comment_json: A file format name. Not translated, in any language or script.
export._comment_csvHelp: Shown under the formats while CSV is chosen. 'Values a folder sets are written into each row' means inherited ports and accounts appear on every connection, because a spreadsheet row has no folder above it.
export.csvHelp: हर कनेक्शन के लिए एक पंक्ति, स्प्रेडशीट या इन्वेंटरी के लिए। फ़ोल्डर जो मान तय करता है, वे हर पंक्ति में लिखे जाते हैं। Remoter इस फ़ाइल को वापस इम्पोर्ट कर सकता है।
export._comment_sshConfigHelp: Shown while OpenSSH config is chosen. 'Host blocks' is the file format's own term; 'ssh' is the command.
export.sshConfigHelp: SSH कनेक्शन Host ब्लॉक के रूप में, कमांड लाइन पर ssh के लिए। बाकी प्रोटोकॉल छोड़ दिए जाते हैं। Remoter इस फ़ाइल को वापस इम्पोर्ट कर सकता है।
export.jsonHelp: ट्री ठीक वैसा ही जैसा वॉल्ट उसे रखता है — फ़ोल्डर, इनहेरिटेंस, सेटिंग्स — स्क्रिप्ट, समीक्षा और वर्ज़न कंट्रोल के लिए।
export._comment_noSecrets: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The heading of a callout. It must say plainly that no secret is written — a translation that hedges it ('most passwords', 'passwords are protected') is wrong.
export.noSecrets: कोई पासवर्ड, प्राइवेट की या पासफ़्रेज़ नहीं लिखा जाता।
export._comment_plaintextBody: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The body of that callout. Both halves are needed: no secrets, AND the file is not encrypted and names every server and account. Reassurance without the second half is misleading.
export.plaintextBody: फिर भी फ़ाइल एन्क्रिप्ट नहीं होती: इसमें आपके सर्वर, उनके पते और उन पर इस्तेमाल होने वाले खाते लिखे होते हैं, और जो भी फ़ाइल पढ़ सकता है वह यह सब पढ़ सकता है।
export._comment_audited: Exporting writes a row into the vault's audit log. Said before the fact, so the row is not a surprise.
export.audited: एक्सपोर्ट ऑडिट लॉग में दर्ज होता है।
export._comment_pathPlaceholder: An example of a file path, shown in an empty field. Adapt it to a path a reader of your language would recognise, but keep it an example and keep it a path.
export._comment_browse: Opens the system save dialog. The ellipsis marks it as leading to another window.
export.browseFailed: सिस्टम का फ़ाइल डायलॉग नहीं खुला। इसके बजाय पाथ टाइप करें।
export._comment_pathMissing: A validation message under the field and on the button's tooltip. Imperative: it says what to do.
export.pathMissing: पहले चुनें कि फ़ाइल कहाँ लिखनी है।
export._comment_busy: Read out while the file is being written, in place of the button's label.
export._comment_doneDetail: {written} is how many connections are in the file and {total} how many there were — they differ when a format cannot describe some of them. {path} is the file (isolated), {size} its size, already formatted.
export.doneDetail: {total, number} में से {written, plural, one {# कनेक्शन} other {# कनेक्शन}} {path} में लिखे गए ({size})।
export._comment_notesTitle: A heading over the list of things the format could not write the way the vault holds them. {count} is how many.
export.notesTitle: {count, plural, one {इस फ़ाइल के बारे में जानने लायक # बात} other {इस फ़ाइल के बारे में जानने लायक # बातें}}
export._comment_notesMore: Under that list, when it was cut short. {count} is how many are not shown.

note._comment_: One line for each thing an export could not write the way the vault holds it. {item}, {folder}, {target} and {written} are names from the user's own tree, isolated; {protocol} is a protocol name such as RDP. Each line says what happened and what it means for the file.
note.unsupportedProtocol: {item} छोड़ दिया गया: OpenSSH config में {protocol} पर चलने वाले कनेक्शन को नहीं लिखा जा सकता।
note.deletedHop: {item}: इसका जंप होस्ट डिलीट हो चुका है, इसलिए कोई रूट नहीं लिखा गया।
note.ambiguousHop: {item}: किसी दूसरे कनेक्शन का नाम इसके जंप होस्ट जैसा ही है, इसलिए गलत मशीन की ओर इशारा करने का जोखिम लेने के बजाय रूट छोड़ दिया गया।
note._comment_hopOutsideExport: The jump host lives in a folder that was not exported. The file mentions it by name, so a person reading it knows; a later import of this one file cannot find it.
note.hopOutsideExport: {item}: इसका जंप होस्ट इस एक्सपोर्ट में नहीं है। रूट में उसका नाम है, लेकिन सिर्फ़ यह फ़ाइल इम्पोर्ट करने पर वह नहीं मिलेगा।
note.hopCredential: {item}: इसके रूट का एक जंप होस्ट अपने अलग क्रेडेंशियल से साइन इन करता है, जिसे यह फ़ॉर्मैट नहीं कह सकता। रूट उसके बिना लिखा गया।
note.hopNotSsh: {item}: इसका रूट ऐसे कनेक्शन से होकर जाता है जो SSH नहीं है, और ssh उसे जंप होस्ट की तरह इस्तेमाल नहीं कर सकता। कोई रूट नहीं लिखा गया।
note._comment_renamed: An OpenSSH config names each host with a short pattern that cannot hold spaces or most punctuation, so the connection got a simpler name in the file.
note.renamed: {item} को {written} के नाम से लिखा गया है, ऐसा नाम जिसे ssh चुन सकता है।
note.folderNameSplits: फ़ोल्डर {folder} के नाम में / है। यह CSV इम्पोर्ट करने पर इसे एक फ़ोल्डर के अंदर दूसरा फ़ोल्डर पढ़ा जाएगा।
note._comment_valueNotWritten: {field} is one of the field nouns below.
note.valueNotWritten: {item}: इसका {field} इस फ़ॉर्मैट में नहीं लिखा जा सकता, इसलिए छोड़ दिया गया।
note.outsideReference: {item} का हवाला {target} से है, जो इस एक्सपोर्ट में नहीं है। फ़ाइल में उसका नाम है, पर वह शामिल नहीं है।

palette._comment_: Ctrl/Cmd+K from anywhere: a search box over the connections, plus a short list of actions. It is a keyboard surface — the labels are what the user types at, so a word that nobody would type is a word that breaks the search.
palette.label: कमांड पैलेट
palette.placeholder: कनेक्शन खोजें, या कोई कमांड टाइप करें…
palette._comment_inputLabel: The accessible name of the search box. Shorter than the placeholder because it is read before every keystroke.
palette._comment_groupConnections: A heading over the search results. Same word as tree.label and for the same reason; they are separate keys because a language may need a different form under a heading.
palette._comment_refining: The search is running again because the query changed. Distinct from 'Searching…', which is the first run into an empty panel.
palette.refining: नतीजे और छाँटे जा रहे हैं…
palette.noResults: “{query}” से कुछ भी मेल नहीं खाता।
palette._comment_count: How many results are shown, out of every connection in the vault. Both are numbers and both are formatted for the locale.
palette._comment_countPending: The total has not arrived yet. The ellipsis stands in for the number that is still coming; do not replace it with a zero.
palette._comment_countUnknown: The total could not be read at all. Says only what is known rather than stating a total that would be wrong.
palette.countUnknown: {count, plural, one {# दिख रहा है} other {# दिख रहे हैं}}
palette.countFailed: कनेक्शन की गिनती पढ़ी नहीं जा सकी
palette._comment_subtitle: The second line of a search result, for the two shapes whose subtitle is a count rather than an address: a folder's children and a group's members. The core sends the number, so the plural category and the digits are this catalogue's to get right. The # is the number itself.
palette._comment_hintSelect: A footer hint beside the Enter key cap. Two outcomes for one key: on a connection it opens a session, on a folder or a credential it selects. Lower case — it is a fragment beside a key, not a sentence.
palette._comment_hintEdit: Beside the Ctrl+Enter key cap. Verb: open the entry in the editor.
palette._comment_hintFilter: Follows the four filter chips (tag:, proto:, host:, user:). Those prefixes are query syntax the core parses and are never translated; this word says what they do.
palette._comment_assurance: SECURITY-CRITICAL. A statement of fact about what the search index contains: secrets are encrypted per field and are never indexed, so a search cannot reach one. Do not weaken it into a promise or a policy ('we do not search secrets') — it is a property of the design.
palette._comment_actionLockVault: The action rows. Each is a command the user runs by pressing Enter on it, and each is matched against what the user typed — so keep the word someone would actually search for at the front.

editor._comment_: The connection editor. Nothing here autosaves and nothing here is read back: the password and the key passphrase can be written and cleared but never shown, which is why so much of this copy is about what a field will do rather than what it holds.
editor._comment_titleEdit: The dialog heading when the entry being edited has no name to show — normally the entry's own name is the heading.
editor._comment_close: The X in the corner. Says which thing closes, because a session tab, the inspector and this dialog can all be on screen at once.
editor._comment_locationPath: Where the entry sits, beside the heading. {path} is a chain of folder names the user created; it is already joined with breadcrumbSeparator.
editor.loadFailed: यह एंट्री लोड नहीं हो सकी
editor.missing: वह एंट्री अब वॉल्ट में नहीं है।
editor._comment_sectionIdentity: Section headings. 'Identity' here means what the entry IS — its name, protocol and address. The login lives under Credentials.
editor._comment_sectionProtocolSettings: The heading over the settings that belong to the connection's protocol rather than to every connection — an RDP domain, a VNC encoding. 'Protocol' here is the word from the Protocol field above it; keep the two the same word.
editor._comment_protocolSettingsLoading: The form for this section is drawn from the protocol adapter's own schema, which is fetched once. Shown while that is in flight — normally too briefly to read.
editor.protocolSettingsLoading: प्रोटोकॉल की सेटिंग्स पढ़ी जा रही हैं…
editor._comment_protocolSettingsSchemaFailed: The title over the failure notice when the schema could not be read. Without it there is nothing to draw: the shape of every control on this section comes from it. Say what could not be read, not what the user should do — the notice carries its own actions.
editor.protocolSettingsSchemaFailed: इस प्रोटोकॉल की सेटिंग्स पढ़ी नहीं जा सकीं।
editor._comment_protocolSettingsUnknown: Introduces the settings below it, which are stored on this connection but are not in the list this build's adapter declares — an import wrote them, or a newer version of Remoter did. They are kept rather than deleted, and they are shown rather than hidden, but this build does not know what they hold and will not offer a control for them. Do not translate this as 'unsupported': they may well be supported, by a build that is not this one.
editor.protocolSettingsUnknown: ये इस कनेक्शन पर सेव हैं, पर इस बिल्ड में इस प्रोटोकॉल की सेटिंग्स का हिस्सा नहीं हैं। इन्हें जैसी हैं वैसी ही रखा जाता है और बिना छेड़े आगे भेज दिया जाता है।
editor._comment_protocolLimits: SECURITY-ADJACENT. One sentence per protocol, naming what this build's adapter does NOT do — so that a missing control reads as an answer rather than as an oversight. Every item is a real gap in the adapter, not a policy: there is no setting for any of them because there is nothing behind them. Do not add to these lists and do not remove from them; they are kept in step with the adapters. 'Remote Desktop Gateway', 'RDP', 'VNC', 'RFB' and 'Tight' are product and protocol names and are never translated.

protocolLimits._comment_rdp: The desktop, the keyboard and the pointer are what RDP carries here. 'Console session' is the /admin session on a Windows server. 'True colour' is 32-bit colour; the frame format has no other depth, so colour depth is not a choice rather than a choice nobody made.
protocolLimits.rdp: इस बिल्ड का RDP डेस्कटॉप, कीबोर्ड और पॉइंटर ले जाता है। यह क्लिपबोर्ड, ड्राइव, प्रिंटर या स्मार्ट कार्ड रीडायरेक्ट नहीं करता, ऑडियो नहीं ले जाता, कोई कंसोल सेशन नहीं खोलता, सिर्फ़ एक ही मॉनिटर चलाता है, और Remote Desktop Gateway से होकर नहीं जाता। रंग-गहराई भी कोई विकल्प नहीं है — हर फ़्रेम 32-बिट ट्रू कलर में ही आता है।
protocolLimits._comment_vnc: 'Ask the server to resize' is the client-initiated desktop resize, which RFB has no standard message for — so the tab scales the picture instead, which is a different thing and worth naming. Reading the remote clipboard is the direction that is missing; pasting into the session is not.
protocolLimits.vnc: इस बिल्ड का VNC Raw एन्कोडिंग देता है और बाक़ी सर्वर पर छोड़ देता है, इसलिए Tight के कम्प्रेशन और क्वालिटी स्तरों के लिए तय करने को कुछ है ही नहीं। यह सर्वर से आकार बदलने को नहीं कह सकता — इसके बजाय टैब तस्वीर को स्केल करता है — और रिमोट क्लिपबोर्ड नहीं पढ़ सकता। VNC में वायर पर कोई खाता नाम होता ही नहीं, इसलिए ऊपर दिया यूज़रनेम सिर्फ़ आपके रिकॉर्ड के लिए रखा जाता है, भेजा नहीं जाता।

editor._comment_settingNote: A line under one particular setting, shown only when that setting's value has a consequence. Each names the cost of the value that is actually set, so none of them is boilerplate.

settingNote._comment_rdpDomain: The mistake this line exists for: an administrator types the domain into the username box, or leaves it out entirely, and the password is then checked against the wrong account. NTLM hashes the account and the domain separately, so DOMAIN\user in the username field is handled — but the two are not interchangeable. Keep the backslash form literal; it is what Windows shows.
settingNote.rdpDomain: Windows डोमेन, जो यूज़रनेम से अलग होता है। लोकल खाते के लिए इसे खाली छोड़ें। DOMAIN\user की तरह लिखा गया यूज़रनेम अपना डोमेन ख़ुद लेकर आता है और इसे ओवरराइड कर देता है।
settingNote._comment_rdpKeyboardLayout: SECURITY-ADJACENT in the sense that it is silent when wrong. Shown under the keyboard layout every time, whatever the value: RDP sends the POSITION of the key that was pressed and the SERVER turns that into a character using the layout named here, so a layout that does not match the keyboard in front of the user produces the wrong characters with no error at either end. That is the whole reason the line exists — name the mechanism, do not turn it into advice. 'Windows' is a product name and is never translated.
settingNote.rdpKeyboardLayout: आप कीबोर्ड पर जो दबाते हैं, Windows उसे इसी लेआउट के हिसाब से अक्षरों में बदलता है। अगर यह उस कीबोर्ड से मेल नहीं खाता जिस पर आप सचमुच टाइप कर रहे हैं, तो रिमोट सेशन में ग़लत अक्षर टाइप होते हैं और कहीं कोई गड़बड़ी दर्ज नहीं होती।
settingNote._comment_rdpNlaOff: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Network Level Authentication is off on this connection. Without it the credentials are sent to whatever answered the port, before the server has proved it is the right machine. State the consequence; do not turn it into advice.
settingNote.rdpNlaOff: इस कनेक्शन पर नेटवर्क स्तर प्रमाणीकरण बंद है, इसलिए पोर्ट का जवाब जिसने भी दिया हो, यह साबित होने से पहले कि वह कौन सी मशीन है, आपके क्रेडेंशियल उसी को भेज दिए जाते हैं।
settingNote._comment_vncFloor: The floor is at its default. Explains what a floor is for, since nothing else on the screen does: without one the server alone decides how old a conversation the two of you have.
settingNote.vncFloor: सबसे पुराना RFB संस्करण जिसे यह कनेक्शन स्वीकार करेगा। RFB में तय यह होता है कि दोनों में से जो कम हो वही चले, इसलिए कोई न्यूनतम न हो तो अकेला सर्वर ही तय करता है कि कितना पीछे जाना है।
settingNote._comment_vncFloorLowered: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The floor has been lowered below 3.8. RFB 3.3 lets the SERVER pick the security type rather than offering a list the client chooses from, and below 3.8 a failed handshake can appear as a connection that simply stops instead of as a reported error. Both halves matter.
settingNote.vncFloorLowered: यह कनेक्शन 3.8 से पुराना RFB संस्करण भी स्वीकार करेगा। 3.3 पर सुरक्षा प्रकार सर्वर ख़ुद चुनता है, आपको कोई सूची नहीं देता, और ठुकराया गया लॉगिन साफ़-साफ़ बताई गई विफलता के बजाय ऐसे कनेक्शन के रूप में सामने आ सकता है जो बस रुक जाता है।
settingNote._comment_vncExclusive: The connection is set to exclusive rather than shared. The consequence is about other people, which is why it is worth a line: connecting will disconnect whoever is already on that screen.
settingNote.vncExclusive: एक्सक्लूसिव: यह सेशन खोलने पर वह हर कोई डिसकनेक्ट हो जाएगा जो पहले से उस स्क्रीन को देख रहा है।
settingNote._comment_vncViewOnly: Input is suppressed on this connection. Say where it is suppressed — locally — because a user who believes the server is refusing their keystrokes will go and change the server.
settingNote.vncViewOnly: सिर्फ़ देखना: कीस्ट्रोक और पॉइंटर की हरकतें यहीं छोड़ दी जाती हैं और सर्वर तक कभी नहीं भेजी जातीं।

editor.name: नाम
editor._comment_protocolNone: Stands where SSH, RDP, VNC or SFTP would, for an entry with no protocol recorded. A placeholder glyph, not a word; change it only if an em dash reads as something else in your script.
editor._comment_protocolFixedHelp: Why the protocol is a badge rather than a menu once the connection exists.
editor.protocolFixedHelp: प्रोटोकॉल कनेक्शन बनाते समय ही चुना जाता है।
editor._comment_password: Both a field label and the name of the third authentication method. Noun.
editor.tagsHelp: कॉमा से अलग करें। टैग ट्री के आर-पार चलते हैं — एक टैग कई फ़ोल्डरों में फैल सकता है।
editor._comment_locationRoot: The breadcrumb for an entry with no folder above it. The root of the tree.
editor._comment_breadcrumbSeparator: Joins folder names into a path: Production / Europe / Web. The glyph only; the space on either side of it is layout and is added by the code. Each name is isolated, so the chain reads in the document direction and this glyph is not flipped.
editor._comment_setHere: Provenance, under a field: this value belongs to this entry and is inherited from nothing. Lower case — it is a fragment under a value, not a sentence.
editor.setHere: इसी कनेक्शन पर तय किया गया
editor._comment_inheritedFrom: Provenance: the value comes from a folder further up. {source} is a folder or credential name the user created, isolated before it arrives.
editor._comment_protocolDefault: Provenance: nobody set this value anywhere; it is what the protocol uses when nothing says otherwise, such as port 22 for SSH.
editor._comment_overridesDefault: Provenance for a field set here that would otherwise have taken the protocol default.
editor.overridesDefault: प्रोटोकॉल के डिफ़ॉल्ट को ओवरराइड करता है
editor._comment_overridesSource: Provenance for a field set here that would otherwise have been inherited. This is the case worth being clear about: the folder still says something different, and this entry is ignoring it.
editor.overridesSource: {source} के मान को ओवरराइड करता है
editor._comment_overrideHere: The button that stops inheriting and gives this entry a value of its own. Imperative, and it is the same phrase on every inheritable field on the screen — keep one wording for all of them.
editor._comment_revertTo: The opposite button: give up this entry's own value and inherit again. {value} is what will apply afterwards — either the inherited value itself (a port, a hostname) or the name of the login it will fall back to.
editor.revertTo: इनहेरिट किए गए पर वापस जाएँ ({value})
editor._comment_revertPlain: The same button when what will apply afterwards cannot be named in a word.
editor.revertPlain: इनहेरिट किए गए पर वापस जाएँ
editor._comment_nothingInherited: Shown in place of a value when nothing above this entry supplies one.
editor._comment_settingRevertToDefault: The 'revert' button on a protocol setting whose fallback is the protocol's own default rather than a folder's value — so 'inherited' would be the wrong word. Same verb as revertPlain; different noun.
editor._comment_settingDefaultDetected: Provenance under a protocol setting nobody has set: the value applying was read off THIS machine rather than chosen by Remoter. Today the only one is the RDP keyboard layout, and {value} is that layout's name. Quiet, not a warning — the value is right; the line is there so the user knows where it came from and that they may change it.
editor.settingDefaultDetected: इस कंप्यूटर से पता चला: {value}। अगर रिमोट सेशन में कोई दूसरा कीबोर्ड चाहिए तो इसे बदल दें।
editor._comment_settingDefaultGuessed: SECURITY-ADJACENT, and the one the origin is carried across the boundary for: Remoter tried to read this from the machine, FAILED, and put a stand-in in place. {value} is the stand-in. Say plainly that it is a guess. The case is the RDP keyboard layout, where a wrong value types the wrong characters and nothing anywhere reports a fault — a user who is not told will conclude their keyboard is broken. Do not soften 'could not' into 'may not have'.
editor.settingDefaultGuessed: Remoter यह नहीं बता सका कि यह कंप्यूटर कौन सा कीबोर्ड इस्तेमाल करता है, इसलिए {value} सिर्फ़ एक अनुमान है। अगर यह ग़लत है, तो रिमोट सेशन में ग़लत अक्षर टाइप होंगे। वही कीबोर्ड चुनें जिस पर आप सचमुच टाइप कर रहे हैं।
editor._comment_settingChoose: The empty entry at the top of a picker whose stored value is not one of the listed ones. It disappears once a value is chosen; it is a prompt, not a value.
editor._comment_settingCustom: The last entry in a picker whose list is a convenience rather than the whole of what the setting accepts — the Windows keyboard layout, where several hundred identifiers exist and only the common ones are listed. Choosing it turns the row into a text box. 'Identifier' because that is what is typed: a number, not a name.
editor._comment_settingUseList: The way back from that text box to the list.
editor._comment_settingOn: The word beside a switched-on setting. A switch with no word beside it reads as on or off only by its colour, which is not a reading.
editor._comment_passwordUnchanged: Placeholder in the empty password box when a password is already stored. It is never read back, so this word is the only thing that says one exists. Leaving the box empty keeps the stored password.
editor._comment_passwordNotSet: The same box when no password is stored.
editor._comment_passwordHelp: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Two facts: the password is encrypted in this vault under the user's master key, and it will never be displayed again. Do not turn 'never shown again' into 'hidden'.
editor.passwordHelp: यह इसी वॉल्ट में आपकी मास्टर कुंजी के तहत सेव होता है। इसे दोबारा कभी नहीं दिखाया जाएगा।
editor._comment_loginInheritedFrom: The username, secret and method are one credential, and this one belongs to a folder above. {source} is that folder's name.
editor._comment_loginShared: The same, for a credential that is not inherited but shared: several connections point at it, so editing it would change all of them. {name} is the credential's name.
editor.loginShared: लॉगिन {name} से आता है, जिसे दूसरी एंट्रियाँ भी इस्तेमाल कर सकती हैं।
editor._comment_loginSharedCredential: Provenance under that read-only login. Fragment, not a sentence.
editor._comment_loginRemove: Takes the login away and leaves the connection with none, which is allowed. Only offered when there is nothing to inherit in its place.
editor._comment_consequenceInherited: SECURITY-ADJACENT. Said once, at the moment it becomes true: this edit will give the connection a login of its own, and the folder's credential is NOT being changed under the user. {source} is the folder. Not a warning — the user is doing something reasonable — but do not delete the second half, which is the part that says what is left alone.
editor.consequenceInherited: सेव करने पर इस कनेक्शन को अपना अलग लॉगिन मिल जाएगा। {source} के पास उसका क्रेडेंशियल जस का तस रहेगा, और उसके नीचे की बाक़ी हर चीज़ के पास भी।
editor._comment_consequenceShared: The same sentence for a shared credential rather than an inherited one. {name} is the credential.
editor.consequenceShared: सेव करने पर इस कनेक्शन को अपना अलग लॉगिन मिल जाएगा। {name} जस का तस रहेगा, और उसे इस्तेमाल करने वाली बाक़ी हर चीज़ भी।
editor.authHelp: यह लॉगिन अपनी पहचान कैसे साबित करता है। यह यूज़रनेम के साथ ही सेव होता है।
editor._comment_authPasswordOnly: {protocol} is a protocol name in capitals — RDP or VNC. Those protocols have no key or agent authentication, so only the password field is offered. SSH and SFTP are protocol names and stay as they are.
editor.authPasswordOnly: {protocol} पासवर्ड से प्रमाणीकरण करता है। कुंजी और एजेंट सिर्फ़ SSH और SFTP के लिए हैं।
editor._comment_agentTitle: The first of the three authentication methods, in order of increasing exposure. 'SSH agent' is the name of the program that holds keys on the user's behalf; it is a product-category name and is not translated.
editor._comment_agentRecommended: A badge beside it. The recommendation is real: with an agent the private key never enters this application.
editor._comment_agentBody: Why it is recommended, in one line. The claim is precise — the key does not enter the process at all — so do not soften it to 'safer'.
editor.agentBody: प्राइवेट कुंजी Remoter के अंदर आती ही नहीं — वह agent के पास रहती है और साइन करने का काम भी वही करता है।
editor._comment_agentFilterLabel: An agent can hold many keys, each with a free-text comment such as ada@laptop. This field narrows the agent to one of them.
editor.agentFilterHelp: वैकल्पिक। जब agent के पास कई कुंजियाँ हों, तो इससे वह उसी कुंजी तक सीमित हो जाता है जिसकी टिप्पणी में यह टेक्स्ट है।
editor._comment_keyTitle: The second authentication method: a private key file, read once and stored in the vault. Noun phrase.
editor._comment_keyBody: Why the bytes are copied into the vault instead of the path being remembered: the connection keeps working when the file moves.
editor.keyBody: कुंजी एक बार पढ़कर इसी वॉल्ट में सेव कर ली जाती है, इसलिए फ़ाइल के हट जाने या मिट जाने के बाद भी कनेक्शन काम करता रहता है।
editor._comment_keyChoose: Opens the system file browser. Imperative.
editor._comment_keyChange: The same button when a key is already stored: pressing it replaces what is there.
editor.keyReading: कुंजी फ़ाइल पढ़ी जा रही है…
editor.keyInspectFailed: वह फ़ाइल प्राइवेट कुंजी के रूप में पढ़ी नहीं जा सकी
editor._comment_keyDialogFailed: The platform's own file browser failed to start. The second sentence matters: nothing was chosen and nothing was sent to the vault, so the user has lost nothing.
editor.keyDialogFailed: सिस्टम का फ़ाइल ब्राउज़र नहीं खुला, इसलिए कोई कुंजी फ़ाइल नहीं चुनी गई। वॉल्ट को कुछ भी नहीं भेजा गया।
editor._comment_keyDialogTitle: The title bar of the system file browser.
editor.keyDialogTitle: इस कनेक्शन के लिए प्राइवेट कुंजी चुनें
editor._comment_keyFilterPrivateKey: A file-type filter in that browser, covering .pem, .key, .ppk and .pk8. Separate from keyTitle because a file browser names file types, not authentication methods.
editor._comment_keyFilterAllFiles: The other filter. It exists because a private key is identified by what is inside it, not by its extension.
editor._comment_keyStored: A badge on a key already sealed into the vault. Fragment, lower case.
editor.keyStoredHelp: इस लॉगिन के लिए एक कुंजी पहले से सेव है। फ़ाइल तभी चुनें जब आप उसे बदलना चाहते हों।
editor._comment_keyEncrypted: A badge stating that the key file is itself protected by a passphrase. The neutral, expected case.
editor._comment_keyNotEncrypted: The badge for a key with no passphrase on it. Carried in a warning tone, so keep it factual rather than alarming — an unprotected key is a legitimate choice on a machine the user controls.
editor._comment_keyPassphraseHelp: SECURITY-CRITICAL. Says where the passphrase goes: into the vault beside the key, once, and never shown again. It is asked for only when the key file says it is encrypted.
editor.keyPassphraseHelp: कुंजी पढ़ने के लिए यह एक बार चाहिए। यह वॉल्ट में कुंजी के साथ ही सेव होता है और दोबारा कभी नहीं दिखाया जाता।
editor._comment_keySize: The size of the chosen key file. Bytes, not kilobytes — a private key is small and the exact figure is a useful sanity check.
editor._comment_errorKeyRequired: Validation, shown after the first attempt to save. Every one of these says what to do next rather than what is wrong.
editor.errorKeyRequired: वह प्राइवेट कुंजी फ़ाइल चुनें जो इस वॉल्ट में सेव करनी है।
editor.errorKeyPending: Remoter के कुंजी फ़ाइल पढ़ लेने का इंतज़ार करें।
editor.errorKeyUnreadable: वह फ़ाइल प्राइवेट कुंजी के रूप में पढ़ी नहीं जा सकी। कोई दूसरी चुनें।
editor._comment_errorPassphraseRequired: The key file says it is encrypted, so it cannot be read without the passphrase.
editor.errorPassphraseRequired: यह कुंजी पासफ़्रेज़ से सुरक्षित है, और उसे पढ़ने के लिए Remoter को वह पासफ़्रेज़ चाहिए।
editor._comment_errorPasswordRequired: SECURITY-CRITICAL. The user switched this login from a key or the agent to a password and typed no password. The second sentence is the consequence: saving replaces the stored key. Do not drop it.
editor.errorPasswordRequired: वह पासवर्ड टाइप करें जो इस लॉगिन को इस्तेमाल करना चाहिए। इसके पास अभी जो कुंजी है, वह रखी नहीं जाएगी — उसकी जगह यह पासवर्ड ले लेगा।
editor._comment_errorPortInvalid: The range is the TCP port range and is not negotiable. The numbers are literal.
editor.errorPortInvalid: पोर्ट 1 से 65535 के बीच की पूर्ण संख्या होती है।
editor._comment_errorSettingRequired: A protocol setting is set on this connection but holds nothing, and its type has no empty value — a number or a choice. Says what to do rather than only what is wrong: the way to have no value here is to hand the setting back, which is the button beside the field.
editor.errorSettingRequired: कोई मान भरें, या बग़ल के बटन से इनहेरिट किए गए मान पर वापस जाएँ।
editor._comment_errorSettingNumber: The setting takes a whole number and what was typed is not one. 'Whole' matters: 1920.5 is not a desktop width.
editor.errorSettingNumber: यह सेटिंग पूर्ण संख्या लेती है।
editor._comment_errorSettingRange: The number is outside what the protocol accepts. The bounds come from the protocol itself — a desktop width is 200 to 8192 because the RDP specification says so — so they are stated rather than left for the user to find by trial. Both are numbers and are formatted for the reader's locale.
editor.errorSettingRange: {min, number} और {max, number} के बीच की कोई संख्या भरें।
editor._comment_errorSettingTooLong: The text is longer than the protocol's field allows. {count} is the limit in characters.
editor.errorSettingTooLong: ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा {count, plural, one {# वर्ण} other {# वर्ण}} इस्तेमाल करें।
editor._comment_errorSettingChoice: The value is not one of the ones this setting accepts. Unlike the keyboard layout, some settings are a closed list and there is no typing your own.
editor.errorSettingChoice: दिए गए मानों में से कोई एक चुनें।
editor._comment_save: The primary button when editing an entry that already exists.
editor._comment_create: The primary button when the entry does not exist yet. A different verb from save on purpose: nothing has been written until it is pressed.
editor._comment_noAutosave: A footer note. Nothing on this screen autosaves, which is the opposite of what most editors do — say it plainly.
editor.noAutosave: “रद्द करें” सब कुछ छोड़ देता है। टाइप करते-करते कुछ भी सेव नहीं होता।
editor._comment_discardTitle: Asked when the user leaves a form with unsaved edits in it.
editor._comment_discardKeep: The safe answer, and the one focus lands on. Imperative: go back to the form.
editor._comment_discardConfirm: The destructive answer. Imperative: throw the edits away.
editor._comment_sectionGateway: The heading of the section for SSH servers a session is forwarded through before it reaches its own host. Use the term sysadmins in your language use for an SSH 'jump host' or 'bastion'.
editor._comment_gatewayHelp: One line of help under the jump host field. The order is the order of travel.
editor.gatewayHelp: पहले जिन SSH सर्वरों से होकर जाना है, क्रम में: पहले तक सीधे पहुँचा जाता है और आख़िरी इस होस्ट तक पहुँचता है।
editor._comment_gatewayDirect: Shown when the chain has no hops: the session connects straight to its host.
editor._comment_gatewayNoneAbove: Under an inherited, empty chain: no folder above sets jump hosts, so the session connects directly.
editor.gatewayNoneAbove: ऊपर का कोई फ़ोल्डर जंप होस्ट तय नहीं करता
editor._comment_gatewayHop: The accessible name of one hop's selector. {position} counts from 1.
editor._comment_gatewayMissing: Shown in a hop's selector when the connection it named has been deleted.
editor._comment_gatewayOption: One option in a hop's selector. {name} is the connection's name, {host} its address; both user data, isolated. The em dash separates them; it is not a word.
editor._comment_gatewayMoveUp: Accessible name of an icon button. {position} counts from 1.
editor.gatewayMoveUp: जंप होस्ट {position} को पहले ले जाएँ
editor.gatewayMoveDown: जंप होस्ट {position} को बाद में ले जाएँ
editor._comment_gatewayNoSsh: Shown when there is no SSH connection to choose as a jump host.
editor.gatewayNoSsh: होकर जाने के लिए कोई SSH कनेक्शन नहीं है। पहले जंप होस्ट को SSH कनेक्शन के रूप में जोड़ें।
editor._comment_gatewayInsideFolder: A folder's jump host is itself inside that folder, so connecting to it would route it through itself. {name} is user data.
editor.gatewayInsideFolder: {name} इसी फ़ोल्डर में है, इसलिए उससे कनेक्ट करने पर वह ख़ुद से होकर जाएगा। उसके अपने कनेक्शन में उसे कोई जंप होस्ट न दें।

_comment_settings: Names for the values a protocol setting can take. The settings' own labels live under `settings.<protocol>.*` and are added with the form that renders them.

settings._comment_ssh: The names of the SSH adapter's own settings, as they appear in the connection editor's 'Protocol settings' section. They label the fields declared in crates/remoter-proto-ssh/src/protocol.rs. Each is a NOUN PHRASE naming the thing, not an instruction — the sentence explaining a setting's consequence is a separate string. 'SSH', 'PTY', 'TERM' and the agent are protocol vocabulary and are not translated where your language's system administrators use the English term.

ssh._comment_terminal_type: The value sent as TERM, which tells the remote shell what the terminal can do. 'xterm-256color' is the default and is a literal identifier.
ssh._comment_columns: The width of the pseudo-terminal requested at connect time, in character cells. The tab resizes it afterwards; this is what it starts at.
ssh._comment_initial_command: A command typed into the shell once it opens, as if the user had typed it. Distinct from exec_command below, which replaces the shell entirely — keep the two clearly different in your language.
ssh.initial_command: लॉगिन के बाद चलाने का कमांड
ssh._comment_exec_command: A single command run INSTEAD of an interactive shell. The session ends when it does.
ssh._comment_environment: Environment variables requested for the session, written one NAME=value per line. Most servers refuse all but a few; that is the server's choice, not Remoter's.
ssh._comment_agent_auth: Whether the SSH agent may be used to authenticate this connection. A switch.
ssh._comment_agent_identity: Narrows which of the agent's identities is offered, by the comment the key carries. Empty means all of them.
ssh._comment_agent_forwarding: SECURITY-CRITICAL as a label: forwarding the agent lets the REMOTE host use the keys it holds. 'Forward' is the established term; keep it.

settings._comment_rdp: The names of the RDP adapter's own settings, labelling the fields declared in crates/remoter-proto-rdp/src/protocol.rs. Noun phrases naming the thing. 'Windows', 'RDP' and 'Network Level Authentication' are product and protocol names and are never translated — though a Windows edition in your language will have its own established wording for Network Level Authentication, and that wording is the right one to use.

rdp._comment_domain: The Windows domain the account belongs to. Empty for a local account.
rdp._comment_workstation: The computer name this client reports to the server. It appears in the server's own logs, which is the reason to set it.
rdp._comment_network_level_authentication: Whether to require Network Level Authentication (CredSSP), which proves the server's identity before any credential is sent. Use the wording Windows itself uses in your language.
rdp._comment_desktop_width: The desktop size asked for at connect time, in pixels.
rdp._comment_keyboard_layout: THE ONE THAT MATTERS. The Windows keyboard layout the server uses to turn the key positions this client sends into characters. The values it offers are named under settings.keyboardLayout above. Label it the way Windows labels its own keyboard setting in your language.
rdp._comment_alternate_shell: A program run instead of the Windows desktop, as RemoteApp does. The wire field really is called the alternate shell.
rdp.alternate_shell: डेस्कटॉप के बजाय चलाने का प्रोग्राम
rdp._comment_work_dir: That program's working directory. Meaningless without the setting above it.

settings._comment_vnc: The names of the VNC adapter's own settings, labelling the fields declared in crates/remoter-proto-vnc/src/protocol.rs. 'VNC', 'RFB' and 'Raw' are protocol names and are never translated. The values these offer — '3.8', 'auto', 'raw', 'local', 'remote' — are wire tokens shown exactly as they stand and are not in this file at all.

vnc._comment_shared: Whether the server may keep other viewers connected. Off means opening this session disconnects them, which is why the line under it says so.
vnc.shared: स्क्रीन दूसरे दर्शकों के साथ साझा करें
vnc._comment_view_only: Whether input is dropped before it is sent. 'Watch' rather than 'read only': what is suppressed is typing and clicking, not seeing.
vnc.view_only: सिर्फ़ देखें, कोई इनपुट न भेजें
vnc._comment_encoding: Which encoding to ask for first when describing screen updates. 'auto' lets the server choose.
vnc._comment_cursor: Whether the pointer is drawn by this computer or arrives as part of the picture. 'local' is smoother; 'remote' is exactly what the server shows.
vnc._comment_rfb_version: The newest RFB version this connection will offer. The ceiling.
vnc._comment_rfb_version_min: The oldest it will accept. The floor — and the one with a consequence, explained in the line beneath it.

settings._comment_keyboardLayout: The names Microsoft gives its keyboard layouts, taken from its published table of keyboard identifiers and input method editors for Windows. They label the identifiers in crates/remoter-proto-rdp/src/layout.rs, and they are read by a user picking the keyboard they are actually typing on — so translate each one to whatever your own Windows edition calls that layout, rather than translating the English words. Turkish Q and Turkish F are two different keyboards, not two spellings of one, and the same goes for every pair that differs only by a bracketed suffix: leave those qualifiers in place, because they are what tells two layouts of one language apart.
